_meta.description: Reference dataset of commodity physical/chemical properties used by the packaging recommendation engine. Values are typical ranges drawn from general food-science literature, not lab measurements of any specific batch. Always check 'confidence' before treating a value as authoritative, and treat 'respiration_rate_class' as applicable to fresh produce only (null for everything else).

confidence_levels.high: Well-established in food science references, low variability across cultivars/sources
confidence_levels.medium: Reasonable typical range, but can vary meaningfully by cultivar, processing, or region
confidence_levels.low: Rough estimate; significant variability or limited reference data

_meta.display_name_hi: Hindi display name for this commodity, shown in the UI when Hindi is selected. The underlying 'id' stays in English/ASCII always — it's a stable key used by the API, database, and ML pipeline, never shown to end users directly.

commodities.name: Banana
commodities.notes: Climacteric fruit; ripens and respires rapidly after harvest, sensitive to ethylene.

commodities.name: Apple
commodities.notes: Shelf life varies widely by cultivar; cold storage extends this significantly beyond the ambient range shown.

commodities.name: Mango
commodities.notes: Climacteric; ripening rate strongly temperature-dependent.

commodities.name: Strawberry
commodities.notes: Highly perishable, non-climacteric, very susceptible to mechanical damage and mold.

commodities.name: Grapes
commodities.notes: Non-climacteric; ambient shelf life estimate is rough since commercial grapes are almost always cold-chained.

commodities.name: Tomato
commodities.notes: Climacteric; ripeness stage at packing strongly affects respiration rate.

commodities.name: Potato
commodities.notes: Long-storing tuber; needs dark, ventilated conditions to prevent sprouting and greening.

commodities.name: Spinach
commodities.notes: Leafy green with very high surface-area-to-volume ratio; wilts fast without humidity control.

commodities.name: Carrot
commodities.notes: Root vegetable; benefits from high-humidity, low-O2 micro-environment to resist wilting.

commodities.name: Onion
commodities.notes: Needs ventilation, not a sealed high-humidity pack, or it will rot/sprout.

commodities.name: Milk (pasteurized, liquid)
commodities.notes: Ambient shelf life assumes standard pasteurization (not UHT/aseptic); refrigeration required almost immediately.

commodities.name: Cheddar cheese
commodities.notes: Hard cheese; ambient shelf life is short without refrigeration, though maturation dulls this somewhat.

commodities.name: Yogurt (plain, cup)
commodities.notes: Live-culture product; acidity slows spoilage but cold chain is still expected.

commodities.name: Butter
commodities.notes: High fat content makes it prone to oxidative rancidity and off-flavor absorption without a barrier layer.

commodities.name: Rice (milled, raw)
commodities.notes: Low-moisture staple; main risks are moisture pickup, insect infestation, and rancidity in the germ layer.

commodities.name: Wheat flour
commodities.notes: Whole wheat flour spoils faster than refined due to higher germ/oil content; range shown is for refined flour.

commodities.name: Lentils (dal, dry)
commodities.notes: Very stable dry pulse; primary risks are moisture pickup and pest infestation.

commodities.name: Sugar (refined, granulated)
commodities.notes: Essentially shelf-stable indefinitely if kept dry; main risk is caking from humidity ingress.

commodities.name: Oats (rolled)
commodities.notes: Higher fat content than other grains makes oxidative rancidity a bigger factor; benefits from an O2 barrier.

commodities.name: Turmeric powder
commodities.notes: Volatile oil and color (curcumin) degrade under light and heat; opaque barrier pack preferred.

commodities.name: Black pepper (ground)
commodities.notes: Ground pepper loses volatile aroma compounds faster than whole peppercorns; needs a good aroma barrier.

commodities.name: Red chili powder
commodities.notes: Color (capsanthin) and pungency degrade under light/heat/oxygen exposure.

commodities.name: Cumin seeds (whole)
commodities.notes: Whole seeds retain aroma/oil much longer than ground spice; still benefits from a moisture/O2 barrier.

commodities.name: Chicken (fresh, raw, whole/cut)
commodities.notes: High-risk perishable; effectively requires continuous cold chain, ambient life is only hours.

commodities.name: Mutton (fresh, raw)
commodities.notes: Fat content varies a lot by cut; ambient shelf life is a rough hours-scale estimate.

commodities.name: Fish (fresh, whole)
commodities.notes: Fat content is highly species-dependent (lean whitefish vs. oily fish); spoils faster than red meat at same temperature.

commodities.name: Shrimp (fresh, raw)
commodities.notes: Very high spoilage risk (enzymatic + microbial); near-freezing cold chain from harvest is standard practice.

commodities.name: White bread (sliced loaf)
commodities.notes: Mold growth is the main failure mode; moisture barrier plus limited O2 ingress both matter.

commodities.name: Biscuits / cookies
commodities.notes: Low moisture but high fat: oxidative rancidity and staling from moisture pickup are the two failure modes.

commodities.name: Cake (frosted)
commodities.notes: Highly variable by frosting/filling type (cream vs. fondant); dairy-based fillings push this toward refrigeration.

commodities.name: Orange
commodities.notes: Non-climacteric citrus; thick rind and low respiration give it good ambient storage life relative to most fresh fruit.

commodities.name: Papaya
commodities.notes: Climacteric; ripens and softens quickly at ambient temperature, similar risk profile to mango/banana.

commodities.name: Pomegranate
commodities.notes: Thick rind gives unusually good ambient storage life for a fresh fruit; whole-fruit values only, arils behave very differently once cut.

commodities.name: Watermelon
commodities.notes: Non-climacteric; whole-fruit values only — cut watermelon spoils within a day or two and needs an entirely different pack format.

commodities.name: Cauliflower
commodities.notes: Cruciferous; moderate respiration and prone to browning/wilting of the curd without humidity control.

commodities.name: Cabbage
commodities.notes: Dense head structure gives notably low respiration and long ambient storage life for a leafy vegetable.

commodities.name: Cucumber
commodities.notes: Very high moisture and thin skin make it prone to shriveling; chilling-sensitive but tracked here at ambient.

commodities.name: Capsicum / bell pepper
commodities.notes: Waxy skin gives reasonable ambient storage life; shrivels and softens as it loses moisture over time.

commodities.name: Paneer (fresh, unripened)
commodities.notes: Fresh unripened cheese, no aging/curing to slow spoilage — behaves like a highly perishable dairy product; refrigeration required almost immediately.

commodities.name: Dairy cream
commodities.notes: Fat content varies widely by cream type (light to heavy); assumes standard pasteurization, not UHT — refrigeration required almost immediately, same caveat as milk_pasteurized.

commodities.name: Sweetened condensed milk (canned/sealed)
commodities.notes: High sugar content and sealed can/tube packaging give it an unusually long ambient shelf life for a dairy product; figure assumes unopened.

commodities.name: Ghee (clarified butter)
commodities.notes: Near-anhydrous milk fat; removing moisture during clarification is precisely what gives it long ambient stability unlike butter, though oxidative rancidity of the fat is still a real long-term risk.

commodities.name: Chickpeas (chana, dry)
commodities.notes: Stable dry pulse, same storage risk profile as lentils_dal: moisture pickup and pest infestation.

commodities.name: Kidney beans (rajma, dry)
commodities.notes: Very stable dry pulse; primary risks are moisture pickup and pest infestation.

commodities.name: Moong dal (split green gram, dry)
commodities.notes: Another common dal variety alongside lentils_dal; same low-moisture stability profile.

commodities.name: Quinoa (dry)
commodities.notes: Notably higher fat content than rice/wheat, so oxidative rancidity of the germ is a bigger factor than for most grains, similar to oats.

commodities.name: Semolina (sooji/rava)
commodities.notes: Coarser durum wheat milling product; similar stability to wheat flour but slightly shorter shelf life is commonly cited.

commodities.name: Coriander powder
commodities.notes: Higher essential-oil content than pepper/chili powder; needs a good aroma/O2 barrier or flavor fades quickly.

commodities.name: Cardamom (green, whole pods)
commodities.notes: Whole pods retain volatile aroma oils much longer than ground spice, similar to whole cumin seeds.

commodities.name: Cloves (whole)
commodities.notes: High eugenol oil content gives whole cloves unusually good aroma stability for a spice.

commodities.name: Mustard seeds (whole)
commodities.notes: Notably high oil content for a whole spice; still shelf-stable long-term but benefits from an O2 barrier against rancidity.

commodities.name: Dried ginger powder (sonth)
commodities.notes: More variable than other ground spices in the dataset depending on drying method; treat this range as a rough estimate.

commodities.name: Fish fillet (fresh, boneless cut)
commodities.notes: More exposed flesh surface area than a whole fish, so ambient shelf life is estimated slightly shorter than fish_fresh_whole; fat content is similarly species-dependent.

commodities.name: Prawns (fresh, raw)
commodities.notes: Essentially the same packaging-relevant profile as shrimp_fresh (a larger crustacean, same enzymatic/microbial spoilage risk) — included separately since they're distinct commercial items in Indian retail.

commodities.name: Processed/cured deli meat (sliced)
commodities.notes: Curing/processing extends refrigerated shelf life considerably versus raw meat, but sliced deli meat still requires a cold chain — ambient figure assumes no refrigeration, same framing as chicken_fresh.

commodities.name: Minced/ground meat (fresh, keema)
commodities.notes: Grinding greatly increases exposed surface area versus a whole cut, so it's generally considered more perishable than mutton_fresh/chicken_fresh at the same temperature.

commodities.name: Dried fish (salted, traditional preservation)
commodities.notes: Salting/sun-drying dramatically extends shelf life versus fresh fish, but moisture and fat content vary hugely by species and drying method — treat as a rough estimate; added salt content (not captured by pH) is part of what inhibits spoilage.

commodities.name: Rusk (toasted bread)
commodities.notes: Double-baked/toasted to drive off moisture, giving it much longer ambient shelf life than the white_bread it's made from — mold risk is greatly reduced, staling/rancidity are the main failure modes.

commodities.name: Muffins (plain)
commodities.notes: Moisture/fat content varies a lot by recipe; similar mold-risk profile to white_bread.

commodities.name: Croissant
commodities.notes: Laminated, high-butter-content pastry; short shelf life from both mold risk (moisture) and rapid staling/rancidity (fat).

commodities.name: Almonds (raw, shelled)
commodities.notes: Very high fat content makes oxidative rancidity the primary failure mode; among the more shelf-stable common nuts.

commodities.name: Cashews (raw, shelled)
commodities.notes: More prone to rancidity than almonds at ambient temperature, so a shorter typical shelf life is commonly cited.

commodities.name: Walnuts (shelled)
commodities.notes: Among the highest-fat common nuts and notably prone to going rancid fastest at ambient temperature without a good O2 barrier.

commodities.name: Peanuts (raw, shelled)
commodities.notes: High fat content drives the same oxidative-rancidity risk as tree nuts.

commodities.name: Raisins (dried grapes)
commodities.notes: Low fat and low water activity from drying/sugar concentration give good ambient stability; main risks are moisture pickup and crystallization.

commodities.name: Dried apricots
commodities.notes: Semi-moist dried fruit (not bone-dry like raisins); low fat, acidic, benefits from a moisture barrier to prevent both drying further and mold growth.

commodities.name: Fruit juice (bottled, pasteurized)
commodities.notes: Assumes standard pasteurization (not UHT/aseptic) — same framing as milk_pasteurized; UHT/aseptic-packed juice is shelf-stable far longer but is a different product/process not modeled here.

commodities.name: Flavored milk (dairy-based, pasteurized)
commodities.notes: Same cold-chain dependency as plain milk_pasteurized; assumes standard pasteurization, not UHT.

commodities.name: Lassi (dairy-based yogurt drink)
commodities.notes: Fermented dairy drink, similar acidity/spoilage profile to yogurt; refrigeration required almost immediately.

commodities.name: Coconut water (packaged, pasteurized)
commodities.notes: Assumes standard pasteurization, not UHT/aseptic tetra-pak (which is a common real format with much longer ambient life) — treat as a rough estimate given how much real products vary by process.

commodities.name: Iced tea (bottled, sweetened, pasteurized)
commodities.notes: Assumes standard pasteurization, not aseptic/UHT; commercial iced tea is often acidified, which gives it a somewhat longer ambient window than milk-based drinks despite the same non-aseptic assumption.

commodities.name: Frozen peas
commodities.notes: Shelf life figure is for frozen (-18C) storage, not room temperature — freezing halts the respiration/spoilage this dataset otherwise tracks via respiration_rate_class, so that field is null here.

commodities.name: Frozen paratha (ready-to-cook flatbread)
commodities.notes: Shelf life figure is for frozen storage, not room temperature. Layered dough often has oil/ghee between layers, raising fat content versus plain bread.

commodities.name: Ice cream
commodities.notes: Shelf life figure is for frozen storage, not room temperature — ice cream melts within hours at ambient and is not a meaningfully packageable state.

commodities.name: Frozen mixed vegetables
commodities.notes: Shelf life figure is for frozen storage, not room temperature; moisture/pH vary by vegetable blend composition.

commodities.name: Frozen french fries (par-fried)
commodities.notes: Shelf life figure is for frozen storage, not room temperature; par-frying before freezing adds oil pickup versus raw potato.

commodities.name: Namkeen (savory fried snack mix)
commodities.notes: Deep-fried, high-oil-content snack; rancidity from repeated-use frying oil is a bigger practical risk than for baked snacks like biscuits, hence a shorter shelf life estimate.

commodities.name: Energy bar (oats/nuts/dried fruit, bound)
commodities.notes: Semi-moist texture (higher moisture than biscuits) combined with nut/fat content gives it a shorter typical shelf life than a fully dry baked snack; formulation varies a lot by brand.

commodities.name: Roasted makhana (fox nuts)
commodities.notes: Fat content depends heavily on whether roasted plain or with oil; low-moisture roasted snack, similar general risk profile to other fried/roasted snacks but typically lower-fat.

commodities.name: Potato chips (fried)
commodities.notes: Very low moisture but very high fat and high surface area (thin slices) make oxidative rancidity the dominant failure mode — needs a strong light/O2 barrier despite not being a wet product.
